elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 11.4 applies "Commencing six (6) months prior to the expiration of the Term ... or upon any termination of this Agreement for any reason"; new 11.5 restates availability "following the expiration or any termination of this Agreement".

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: The only six-month period in 11.4 requires "the written request of Customer, given at least 100 days prior to expiration of the Term" — a condition tied solely to anticipated expiry, so it does not run after a mid-term termination. Inserted 11.5 quantifies only ninety (90) days. To reach preferred, state that Termination Assistance is available for up to six (6) months following any expiry or termination without the 100-day pre-expiry request condition.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: 11.4: "all Expenses and charges for Termination Assistance shall be computed in accordance with M&I's then-current rates for such products, materials and services."

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: New 11.5: "M&I shall export and deliver to Customer all Customer Data then in M&I's possession within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination."

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: 11.5 requires export and delivery but specifies no format; no "commonly used, machine-readable format" language appears anywhere. Add a format qualifier to the 30-day export obligation.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion or written certification obligation exists; 17.5 addresses only security safeguards. Add a clause requiring M&I to delete Customer Data after return and certify deletion in writing.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 11.4 triggers on expiration or "any termination of this Agreement for any reason", and 11.5 expressly attaches to "the expiration or any termination of this Agreement".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: New 11.5: "Termination Assistance shall be available to Customer for at least ninety (90) days following the expiration or any termination of this Agreement" — unconditional and post-termination, curing the 100-day pre-expiry request defect.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: New 11.5 obliges M&I to "export and deliver to Customer all Customer Data then in M&I's possession within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination"; temporal anchor runs from expiry/termination, not from a request.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the inserted 11.5 supplies an unconditional at-least-90-day Termination Assistance period keyed to any expiry or termination and a 30-day Customer Data export obligation, while 11.4 already carries the expiry-or-any-termination trigger.

Preferred level is not complete: the six-month period in 11.4 remains conditioned on a written request 100 days before expiration (unavailable after mid-term termination), and there is no machine-readable format requirement and no post-return deletion certification.

Minimality holds: the redline is a single concise insertion limited to the two missing fallback elements; no text was deleted, the existing six-month expiry mechanic and the favourable then-current-rates/no-obligation-to-take-assistance language are retained, and no extras (survival tail, expense allocation, procedures, deletion certification) were added.

Intent preserved: 11.5 uses the defined term "Termination Assistance" and the defined "Customer Data" from 17.1, leaves no dangling cross-reference or undefined trigger, and does not contradict 11.4's continued-Services mechanic, expense estimate, or 17.5 security duty.
Finding status "deviation" is supportable because the pre-existing clause failed the fallback on assistance duration after mid-term termination and lacked any data return/export obligation.
